# References to mine — auditing-data-pipeline-health

## From category #41

### Key references

- **dbt — `exposures`, `sources`, model `versions`/`deprecation_date`, and the artifact files (`manifest.json`, `run_results.json`, `sources.json`)** — https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/build/exposures → mine: the repo already holds a machine-readable dependency graph. `exposures` declare the downstream consumers a `ref()` graph cannot see (dashboards, ML jobs, notebooks); `manifest.json` gives every model, test, and edge; `run_results.json` and `sources.json` give the last run's test outcomes and source-freshness results. Where those artifacts are present, an audit stops guessing and starts counting.
- **Open Data Contract Standard / Data Contract Specification + `datacontract-cli`** — https://datacontract.com/ → mine: the contract is a versioned artifact with a schema, quality expectations, an **owner**, and an SLA — so it is auditable as an artifact in its own right: does every published dataset have one, does it name a live owner, and has anything actually tested the dataset against it (`datacontract test`) rather than merely storing it?
- **Confluent Schema Registry — subject compatibility configuration** — https://docs.confluent.io/platform/current/schema-registry/fundamentals/schema-evolution.html → mine: compatibility is per-subject *configuration*, so it drifts independently of any schema change — a subject set to `NONE` (or left at a default nobody chose) gates nothing, and the repo's `.avsc`/`.proto` can silently diverge from the version actually registered. Both are standing conditions, invisible in a diff.
- **Andrew Jones — *Driving Data Quality with Data Contracts* (Packt, 2023)** → mine: a contract without an owner and an enforcement point is documentation. The audit question is not "is there a contract" but "is anything failing when it is violated, and does a named human hear about it."
- **Barr Moses / Monte Carlo — data observability's five pillars** — https://www.montecarlodata.com/blog-what-is-data-observability/ → mine: **freshness, volume, distribution, schema, lineage** as the coverage matrix to audit *against*. Score the model graph by which pillars have no expectation at all, rather than reviewing monitors one at a time.
- **Michael Feathers — *Working Effectively with Legacy Code*** → mine: "legacy code is code without tests," applied to the data plane — an untested model is one nobody can safely change. Rank by **downstream fan-out**: an untested model with thirty dependents is a different finding from an untested leaf.
- **#30 enforcement-apparatus parity — see that section.** A permanently-failing `severity: warn` test and a `continue-on-error` compatibility check are the data plane's version of an unjustified suppression and a soft-failed gate; #30 owns the general pattern, #41 the data-plane instance, and neither should re-derive the other.
- **#39 decision-record currency — the structural precedent.** Same shape one cluster over: an authoring-time lens (#29/#40) paired with a scheduled currency audit (#39/#41) that asks only whether *time* has invalidated something already declared.
